# The Single-Tax Model and the Second-Order Condition {#sec-app-soc-model}

This appendix presents the single-tax model that @sec-model nests, and derives the second-order condition (SOC) for the firm's problem, which translates into the curvature restriction on the detection function $q(e)$ used throughout the paper.

## The single-tax model {#sec-app-single-tax}

The single-tax model keeps every assumption of @sec-model except one: a single rate $\tau$ applies to both sales and purchases. The firm solves
$$
\begin{aligned}
  \max_{K,L,M,e}\;\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}] = \;&(1-\tau)\big(P_tK_{it}^{\alpha_K}L_{it}^{\alpha_L}M_{it}^{\beta}\exp(\omega_{it})-\rho_tM_{it}\big)-r_tK_{it}-w_tL_{it}\\
  &+\big[1-q(e_{it})\big]\tau\rho_te_{it}-q(e_{it})\phi\tau\rho_te_{it}-c_{it}(e_{it},\omega_{it}),
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-app-st-profit}
which is @eq-profit with $\tau_S=\tau_P=\tau$. The tax rate drops out of the materials first-order condition,
$$
\beta K_{it}^{\alpha_K}L_{it}^{\alpha_L}M_{it}^{\beta-1}\exp(\omega_{it})=\rho_t/P_t,
$$ {#eq-app-st-foc-m}
so the gross log share, $\ln(\rho_tM_{it}/P_tY_{it})=\ln\beta-\varepsilon_{it}$, takes the place of the net share in @eq-share-net. The evasion first-order condition is @eq-foc-e with $\tau$ in place of $\tau_P$,
$$
\tau\rho_t\big[1-(1+\phi)\big(q(e_{it})+q'(e_{it})e_{it}\big)\big]=\frac{\partial c_{it}(e_{it},\omega_{it})}{\partial e_{it}},
$$ {#eq-app-st-foc-e}
and firms for which $\tau\rho_t\le\partial c_{it}(0,\omega_{it})/\partial e_{it}$ do not overreport.

## The second-order condition {#sec-app-soc}

### Setup

Recall the firm's problem in the two-tax model, @eq-profit, and its two first-order conditions, @eq-foc-m and @eq-foc-e. For a candidate solution $(K_{it},L_{it},M_{it},e_{it})$ to be a maximum, the Hessian of expected profit must be negative semi-definite at that point.

### The Hessian is block-diagonal

Two features of the model make the Hessian easy to sign.

First, $M_{it}\perp e_{it}$: neither the materials FOC (@eq-foc-m) nor the evasion FOC (@eq-foc-e) contains the other's choice variable, so every cross-partial between $e_{it}$ and $(K_{it},L_{it},M_{it})$ is zero. Second, the production function $Y_{it}=K_{it}^{\alpha_K}L_{it}^{\alpha_L}M_{it}^\beta\exp(\omega_{it}+\varepsilon_{it})$ is Cobb-Douglas, hence strictly concave in $(K_{it},L_{it},M_{it})$ jointly. The Hessian is therefore block-diagonal,
$$
\nabla^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]=
\begin{bmatrix}
\dfrac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial e_{it}^2} & 0 & 0 & 0\\[4pt]
0 & \dfrac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial M_{it}^2} & \dfrac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial M_{it}\partial L_{it}} & \dfrac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial M_{it}\partial K_{it}}\\[4pt]
0 & \dfrac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial L_{it}\partial M_{it}} & \dfrac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial L_{it}^2} & \dfrac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial L_{it}\partial K_{it}}\\[4pt]
0 & \dfrac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial K_{it}\partial M_{it}} & \dfrac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial K_{it}\partial L_{it}} & \dfrac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial K_{it}^2}
\end{bmatrix}
$$ {#eq-app-soc-hessian}

with a single nonzero entry in the first row and column. Negative definiteness requires the leading principal minors to alternate in sign (odd-order minors negative, even-order positive). Since the lower $3\times3$ block is already negative definite (strict concavity of the Cobb-Douglas production function in $K_{it},L_{it},M_{it}$), the *only* condition the evasion margin adds to the firm's problem is that the first leading principal minor — the top-left scalar entry — is itself negative:
$$
\frac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial e_{it}^2}<0.
$$

The capital, labour, and materials choices place no restriction on the evasion technology, and vice versa; the SOC for $e_{it}$ can be analyzed entirely on its own.

### The scalar condition

Differentiating the evasion FOC (@eq-foc-e) once more with respect to $e_{it}$,
$$
\frac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial e_{it}^2}=-\tau_P\rho_t(1+\phi)\Big(2q'(e_{it})+e_{it}q''(e_{it})\Big)-\frac{\partial^2c_{it}(e_{it},\omega_{it})}{\partial e_{it}^2}<0.
$$ {#eq-app-soc-full}

Rearranging, the SOC holds whenever
$$
\tau_P\rho_t(1+\phi)\Big(2q'(e_{it})+e_{it}q''(e_{it})\Big)+\frac{\partial^2c_{it}(e_{it},\omega_{it})}{\partial e_{it}^2}>0,
$$
a sum of two terms. It is therefore *sufficient* — not necessary — that either term alone be strictly positive:
$$
\frac{\partial^2c_{it}(e_{it},\omega_{it})}{\partial e_{it}^2}\ge0
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
\tau_P\rho_t(1+\phi)\Big(2q'(e_{it})+e_{it}q''(e_{it})\Big)\ge0.
$$ {#eq-app-soc-split}

**Under this paper's headline cost function**, $c_{it}(e_{it},\omega_{it})=e_{it}\exp\{\delta_0-\delta_1\omega_{it}+\delta_2\omega_{it}^2+\psi_{it}\}$ — linear in $e_{it}$ — the first term is identically zero, $\partial^2c_{it}/\partial e_{it}^2=0$. The cost function therefore contributes nothing toward satisfying the SOC on its own; the entire burden falls on the second condition, the curvature of the detection function.

### The curvature restriction

Since $\tau_P\rho_t(1+\phi)>0$, the second condition in @eq-app-soc-split reduces to $2q'(e_{it})+e_{it}q''(e_{it})\ge0$. Economic theory imposes $q'(e_{it})>0$ (detection is increasing in overreporting) and $e_{it}>0$ for an interior evader, so dividing through by $q'(e_{it})e_{it}>0$ gives
$$
-\frac{q''(e_{it})}{q'(e_{it})}\,e_{it}<2.
$$ {#eq-app-soc-final}

This is a restriction on the **curvature of $q$ alone** — a firm's evasion cost never enters, given the linear-in-$e$ specification above. It says $q'$ may decline as $e_{it}$ rises (a concave detection function), but not too fast relative to its own level: the semi-elasticity of the marginal detection probability with respect to $e_{it}$ must exceed $-2$.

### Application to the candidate detection functions

@tbl-app-soc-forms applies @eq-app-soc-final to the headline detection function of @sec-counterfactual and to the three functional forms considered in @sec-model.

| | $q(e)$ | $q''(e)$ | $-q''e/q'$ | SOC holds when |
|:--|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Scaled power (headline) | $(e/\kappa\bar M)^k$, $0<k<1$ | $k(k-1)(e/\kappa\bar M)^{k-2}/(\kappa\bar M)^2$ | $1-k$ | always ($0<1-k<1$) |
| Linear | $\min\{\lambda e,1\}$ | $0$ | $0$ | always |
| Concave | $1-e^{-\lambda e}$ | $-\lambda^2e^{-\lambda e}$ | $\lambda e$ | $\lambda e<2$ |
| Convex | $\min\{(\lambda e)^k,1\}$, $k>1$ | $k(k-1)\lambda^2(\lambda e)^{k-2}$ | $1-k$ | always ($k>1\Rightarrow1-k<0<2$) |

: Second-order condition by functional form of $q(\cdot)$ {#tbl-app-soc-forms}

**Scaled power detection, $q(e)=(e/\kappa\bar M_{j,t-1})^k$, $0<k<1$** (headline specification, @sec-counterfactual): with $x=e/(\kappa\bar M_{j,t-1})$, $q'(e)=kx^{k-1}/(\kappa\bar M_{j,t-1})$ and $q''(e)=k(k-1)x^{k-2}/(\kappa\bar M_{j,t-1})^2$, so $-q''e/q'=1-k\in(0,1)$. The SOC holds at every interior point, for any $0<k<1$ and any scale; the binding constraint is the FOC's own ceiling $x<(1+k)^{-1/k}$.

**Linear detection, $q(e)=\min\{\lambda e,1\}$**: $q''(e)=0$ on the interior, so $-q''e/q'=0<2$ unconditionally — the SOC holds at every interior point, with no restriction on $\lambda e$ beyond the FOC's own ceiling ($\lambda e<1/2$, from @sec-model).

**Concave detection, $q(e)=1-e^{-\lambda e}$**: $q'(e)=\lambda e^{-\lambda e}$ and $q''(e)=-\lambda^2e^{-\lambda e}$, so $-q''e/q'=\lambda e$. The SOC requires $\lambda e<2$ — a genuine restriction, distinct from (and, for this functional form, looser than) the FOC's own ceiling $\lambda e<1$ derived in @sec-model. Since $\lambda e<1\implies\lambda e<2$, the FOC ceiling is the binding constraint in practice; the SOC is automatically satisfied wherever the FOC has an interior solution at all.

**Convex detection, $q(e)=\min\{(\lambda e)^k,1\}$, $k>1$**: $q'(e)=k\lambda(\lambda e)^{k-1}$ and $q''(e)=k(k-1)\lambda^2(\lambda e)^{k-2}$, so $-q''e/q'=1-k$. Since $k>1$, this is always negative, hence always less than $2$ — convex detection satisfies the SOC unconditionally, for any $k>1$.

**Summary.** All four detection functions satisfy the second-order condition on the relevant part of their domain — scaled power, linear and convex unconditionally, concave provided $\lambda e<2$, which is already implied by that function's own FOC-ceiling. The choice among them is therefore not disciplined by the SOC; it is a modelling choice about the detection technology, addressed on economic grounds in @sec-counterfactual.

The derivation carries over to the single-tax model (@sec-app-single-tax) with $\tau$ in place of $\tau_P$: the rate scales the curvature term but does not change its sign, so @eq-app-soc-final is the same condition in both models.
